title: Range Rover L405
verdict: An aluminium-bodied air-sprung limousine that will still claw up a rutted hillside if you ask nicely. Buy one with a service history thicker than its door cards, and a warranty for when it doesn't.

paragraphs: The fourth-generation Range Rover broke cover at the 2012 Paris Motor Show and did something no full-size 4x4 had done before: it threw away the steel. Land Rover calls the L405 the first production SUV with an all-aluminium monocoque, and the diet was dramatic — the body-in-white was 39 percent lighter and the whole truck shed about 420 kg (926 lb) against the steel [[range-rover/l322|L322]]. It still had a two-speed transfer box, cross-linked air springs and a 900 mm wading depth. It was simply built from the same stuff as a beer can.

story.heading: LIGHTER, STIFFER, POSHER
paragraphs: Gerry McGovern's design team kept the floating roof, the clamshell bonnet and the upright glasshouse, then smoothed everything else. Underneath, the aluminium shell was built in a new all-aluminium facility at Solihull, using a high-strength alloy with up to 50 percent recycled content. The weight saving went straight into performance and economy: launch engines were a supercharged 5.0 V8, a 3.0 TDV6 and a 4.4 SDV8, all driving through a ZF eight-speed automatic and a Magna Steyr DD295 two-speed transfer case with a 50/50 torque split.

Off-road, the numbers moved the right way. In a UK road test of the launch TDV6, Land Rover quoted 303 mm of ground clearance (up 17 mm), a 900 mm wading depth (up 200 mm), and approach and departure angles of 34.7 and 29.6 degrees. Terrain Response 2 could now read the surface itself and choose between grass/gravel/snow, mud, sand and rock crawl. It would also back off the active anti-roll bars to let the wheels droop when it sensed the truck was off the tarmac.

story.heading: STRETCHED, HYBRIDISED, FACELIFTED
paragraphs: The range grew sideways for nine years. A long-wheelbase version, 200 mm longer between the axles at 3,122 mm, arrived at the 2013 Los Angeles show. A supercharged 3.0 V6 joined in 2014, an SDV6 diesel-electric hybrid followed, and Special Vehicle Operations turned the 5.0 V8 up to 550 PS, then 565 PS, for the SVAutobiography Dynamic. America finally got a diesel, the 254 hp Td6, for the 2016 model year. It was rated at 22 mpg city and 28 highway, against 14 and 19 for the supercharged V8.

The 2018 facelift brought a four-bar grille, new LED lights, thicker glass, and a second touchscreen in place of the climate knobs. The P400e plug-in hybrid followed, pairing a 2.0-litre Ingenium four with a 13.1 kWh battery and an 85 kW motor for 404 PS. Late trucks gained Ingenium straight-sixes, including a 3.0 mild-hybrid petrol for the 2020 model year. One planned derivative never made it: the three-door, 999-unit SV Coupé, shown at Geneva in 2018, was cancelled in January 2019 for financial reasons.

story.heading: THE CATCH
paragraphs: All that cleverness has a price, and second owners pay it. Specialist guides single out pre-2015 cars for the most electrical and body faults. The 3.0 TDV6 family is known for crankshaft and bearing failures, which a 2014 Land Rover bulletin blamed mainly on bearing shells being located wrongly or rotating. The supercharged 5.0 V8 eats timing-chain guides and cracks its plastic coolant pipes, and the air suspension wants compressors and struts. NHTSA lists keyless door-latch recalls for 2013–2016 trucks and front-knuckle cracking recalls for 2014–2017 trucks. None of that stops a sorted L405 being a superb, genuinely capable expedition limo — exactly why Lucky8 built a lifted, winched, rock-slidered 'Project L405' out of a supercharged one.

story.heading: LEGACY
paragraphs: The L405 ran from 2012 to 2021, which Top Gear noted is an age in motoring terms, and the Velar, named after the 1967 prototypes, was spun off during its lifetime. It was replaced by the [[range-rover/l460|L460]] in late 2021. For off-roaders it is now the newest full-size Range Rover with real aftermarket support: lift rods, rock sliders, hidden winch mounts and 285-section all-terrains. Treat it like the 2.3-tonne computer it is, and it will go most places a [[land-cruiser/200-series|Land Cruiser 200]] goes — just more quietly, and with more dashboard messages.

callout.label: SIDEBAR · 2015 ROYAL COMMISSION
callout.title: The topless Range Rover built for the Queen
paragraphs: In June 2015 Land Rover delivered a one-off 'State Review' Range Rover for Queen Elizabeth II. It was based on the long-wheelbase L405 Hybrid, with a 3.0 SDV6 diesel and an electric motor making 335 hp and 700 Nm, and it could run in pure electric mode. The rear passenger compartment had no roof, so the monarch could stand and wave. Land Rover Design built it with engineering input from Special Vehicle Operations.

It made its royal debut in Cardiff, when the Queen presented new Colours to the Royal Welsh Regiment. It was the fourth State Review vehicle from Land Rover: the first was a 1953 Series I, and this one replaced the State Review Range Rover in service since 2002.

engineering_intro: The L405 is a unibody truck with no separate frame. The structure is a riveted and bonded aluminium monocoque, sprung on cross-linked air springs at all four corners and driven full-time through a two-speed transfer case. It is light for its size, and it was properly engineered for off-road work. It is also completely dependent on its electronics: ride height, roll control, traction and even the transfer-case logic all go through modules that want a diagnostic tool, not a spanner.

engineering.note: Body-shell 39% lighter; whole truck about 420 kg lighter than the steel L322.
Access, normal and off-road heights plus automatic levelling; adaptive dampers and hydraulic anti-roll (Dynamic Response).
Permanent 4WD, 50/50 torque split, high and low range.
Fitted to every engine in the range.
Auto-detects surface; grass/gravel/snow, mud, sand, rock crawl; hill descent control and hill start assist.
Up 200 mm on the L322; 303 mm max ground clearance quoted at launch (TDV6).

generations_table.note: US mainstay; 375 PS naturally aspirated 5.0 in some markets. Timing chain and coolant pipes are the watch items.
Shares the supercharger-isolator and plastic-coolant-pipe weaknesses of the V8 family.
The economical pick; crank and bearing failures are documented on the TDV6 family.
Rated by specialists as good and reliable; watch EGR and turbo breather leaks.
35 kW motor in the gearbox; PistonHeads dates UK availability to 2015. Basis of the Queen's State Review car.
13.1 kWh battery and 85 kW motor; arrived with the four-bar-grille facelift.
SVO flagship; 565 PS cars quoted at 0–60 mph in 4.3 s.

buying_checks.head: Check every recall is closed
buying_checks.body: NHTSA lists keyless door-latch recalls for 2013–2016 trucks (doors may unlatch) and front-suspension knuckle recalls for 2014–2017 trucks (the upper knuckle joint can crack). AutoTrader.ca counted at least 19 safety recalls on this generation in Canada. Trucks that left the dealer network early are the most likely to have open campaigns. Run the VIN.

buying_checks.head: Be extra careful with pre-2015 trucks
buying_checks.body: PistonHeads' L405 guide says early cars had the most electrical and body problems. It advises a warranty, saying Land Rover's own cover for early cars costs around £1,400 a year after a free inspection. Panel fit on the rear doors, tailgate and bonnet is a known weak spot, and so are door seals.

buying_checks.head: Listen to the front end on a rough road
buying_checks.body: Coast and brake moderately over broken tarmac. Clunks or pops point to worn front track control arms or rear lower arms (around £700 fitted as a pair, per PistonHeads) — or, on 2014–2017 trucks, to the knuckle recall. AutoTrader.ca says not to take delivery of one with unusual front-end noise.

buying_checks.head: Watch the ride height overnight
buying_checks.body: Compressors fail and air springs split, and PistonHeads calls both 'known things.' Look for a corner that sags after standing, a compressor that runs constantly, or suspension faults on the dash. Check that every height mode works: access, normal and off-road.

buying_checks.head: Cold-start a 5.0 V8 yourself
buying_checks.body: A rattle lasting a second or two on a cold start is the classic sign of tired timing-chain guides and tensioners, particularly on 2010–2014 engines. Fault codes P0016–P0019 come later. A metallic rattle at idle can instead be the supercharger coupler or isolator. Look for coolant loss too: the plastic crossover pipes crack.

buying_checks.head: Ask how the diesel was serviced
buying_checks.body: TDV6/SDV6 crank-bearing failures are documented in Land Rover bulletin SSM71816 and in owner threads. Owners suspect oil sludging under long intervals and the wrong oil grade play a part. Ask for regular servicing with the correct oil. On the 4.4 SDV8, check for EGR faults and oily turbo breather pipes (up to £850 to replace).

buying_checks.head: Test the screens and switches
buying_checks.body: Infotainment freezes, dead cameras and Bluetooth faults are common and often fixed by software. If the head unit goes black or won't boot, assume an expensive repair until proved otherwise. Check the start/stop and steering-wheel buttons, the interior door releases, and the rotary gear selector, which can fail to rise.

buying_checks.head: Look at the wheels, and the transfer-case history
buying_checks.body: PistonHeads says the 22-inch wheels are soft and buckle on potholes, so check them for bends. AutoTrader.ca advises that any non-factory wheels come from a reputable brand and be rated for the truck's weight. Transfer-box and differential oil should be changed at around 30,000 miles, so ask for proof.

repairs.title: Front air strut replacement
repairs.time: ≈ 1–2 hours per side (forum labour estimate for full-size Range Rover struts)
repairs.cost: Front strut about $730–$830 (Lucky8 BWI/OE listings), plus labor
repairs.symptoms: One front corner sitting low after standing, a hiss when the truck lowers to access height, the compressor working overtime, or air-suspension faults that come back after recalibration.
repairs.fix: Relieve the system pressure (it runs up to 10 bar) and disconnect the battery. With the wheels straight, raise the truck, support it safely and remove the wheel. Unplug the strut's electrical connector, release the air line and remove its fitting, then remove the sensor-wire and brake-line bracket and the lower strut bolt. Unhook the anti-roll bar link from the strut clevis and separate the upper control arm ball joint from the knuckle. Remove the top mount nuts, swing the knuckle out and lift the strut out. To fit: leave the air fitting on the new strut, install the strut and lower bolt, reconnect the upper arm, clevis, sway-bar link and brackets, fit the top bolts, then remove the shipping pin and push the air line home until it locks. Plug in the connector, torque everything to factory spec, refit the wheel and recalibrate the ride heights.
repairs.tools: Jack and stands · sockets and ball-joint separator · Arnott ASE-3756 (new electronic) or AS-3067 RH / AS-3068 LH (remanufactured, 2013–2018), or OE LR079515 RH · diagnostic tool with air-suspension calibration (e.g., GAP IID)

repairs.title: Air-suspension lift rods (height-sensor links)
repairs.symptoms: Not a fault — it's the cheapest lift on the planet. The truck sits too low for bigger tyres or rough tracks, or scrapes its sills in ruts.
repairs.fix: Remove the factory ride-height sensor rods at each corner and fit the longer links in their place: short rods at the front, long rods at the rear. The links fool the sensors into reading the truck as lower than it is, so the air springs raise every height mode by 1, 1.5 or 2 inches depending on the kit. No coding is needed and Terrain Response keeps working. Get a wheel alignment afterwards.
repairs.tools: Basic hand tools · Proud Rhino PR25DEF-1 (1 in), PR25DEF-1.5 (1.5 in) or PR25D5 (2 in) lift rods · alignment afterwards

repairs.title: Front lower control arms (clunk fix)
repairs.cost: Around £700 fitted for the common arm pair (PistonHeads); arms from about $290 a pair aftermarket, $785 genuine, $489 polybushed
repairs.symptoms: Knocks or clunks from the front over broken surfaces and under moderate braking; vague steering; uneven tyre wear.
repairs.fix: First run the VIN for the 2014–2017 front-knuckle recall, because a cracking upper knuckle joint can also make noises and is fixed free by dealers. If the knuckles are clear, support the truck on stands, remove the wheel, unbolt the lower arm from the knuckle and the subframe, swap in the new arm, and do the final bush torque with the suspension at ride height. Recalibrate the ride height if a height sensor was disturbed, then align.
repairs.tools: Jack and stands · large sockets and breaker bar · ball-joint separator · LR072469 (LH) / LR072471 (RH) arms, or Lucky8 polybushed kit NFLCKPB · alignment afterwards

repairs.title: 5.0 supercharged cooling-pipe and water-pump refresh
repairs.time: Varies — the rear crossover pipe sits under the supercharger
repairs.cost: Shop price about CA$1,800–3,200 for the pipes (supercharger removal), plus CA$900–1,500 for a water pump; ARC050 aluminium pipe kit $199
repairs.symptoms: Unexplained coolant loss, sweet smell, weeping at the back of the engine or around the thermostat housing. Plastic pipes typically go around 100,000 km and water pumps around 80,000–140,000 km.
repairs.fix: Drain the coolant and remove the supercharger to reach the valley. Replace the factory plastic rear crossover pipe, front Y-tube, oil-cooler-to-water-pump adapter and front crossover bypass with aluminium parts. Do the water pump and thermostat housing while it's apart. Refit the supercharger with new gaskets, then refill and bleed the system. The supplier recommends professional installation.
repairs.tools: Full socket set and torque wrench · coolant and drain pan · ARC050 kit (LR122709/LR109402 rear crossover, LR092992 Y-tube, LR028136 adapter, LR090630 bypass) or SCV85LAUCK kit with water pump and aluminium thermostat housing

parts.name: ARC050 5.0 supercharged aluminium coolant pipe kit
SCV85LAUCK cooling kit: alloy pipes + water pump + thermostat (5.0 SC)
L405 5.0 water pump (search)

repairs.title: 5.0 V8 timing chains, guides and tensioners
repairs.cost: About CA$4,500–7,500 at a specialist; genuine 34-piece kit $1,599
repairs.symptoms: A rattle for a second or two on a cold start, later joined by cam-timing codes P0016, P0017, P0018 or P0019.
repairs.fix: Lock the engine at the correct position with the JLR timing tools before anything comes apart. Replace both cam chains, the tensioners and blades, both guides, the auxiliary drive chain with its tensioner and guide, and the cam lubricating jets, then refit with new rocker-cover gaskets and spark-plug seals. Don't reuse old tensioners or guides: reusing tired parts is the shortcut that brings the truck back on a hook.
repairs.tools: JLR camshaft and crank locking tools · torque wrench · Lucky8 5LTCK genuine kit (chains LR032048, tensioners LR051008, blades LR051013, guides LR051011/LR051012, aux chain LR032087)

parts.name: 5LTCK genuine 5.0 V8 timing chain kit, 34 pieces (L405)
5.0 V8 timing chain kit (search)

repairs.title: Supercharger coupler / isolator
repairs.time: Varies — the snout must come apart
repairs.cost: About CA$900–1,500 for the isolator; CA$2,000–2,800 for a full snout rebuild
repairs.symptoms: A metallic rattle or knock from the front of the engine at idle, often mistaken for timing chain; a louder-than-normal whine means dry snout bearings.
repairs.fix: Rule out the timing chain first with a cold-start listen and a scan for cam-timing codes. Then remove the supercharger snout, replace the spring-type isolator or coupler and, if they're noisy, the snout bearings, and reassemble with a new gasket. One supercharger rebuilder says the stock spring-type isolator usually starts failing from around 50,000 miles. Check isolator/coupler fitment for your engine's build year before ordering.
repairs.tools: Sockets and torque wrench · snout gasket · 5.0 supercharger repair kit (Lucky8 lists LR088564)

parts.name: Supercharger 5.0 repair kit LR088564
5.0 supercharger isolator / coupler (search)

repairs.title: Auxiliary stop/start battery
repairs.cost: About $288 for the AGM auxiliary battery (Lucky8)
repairs.symptoms: Stop/start that works only sometimes or not at all, rough or slow restarts, low-voltage warnings and odd infotainment behaviour.
repairs.fix: Test the main battery first, since it is separate and a weak one also upsets stop/start. If the auxiliary battery is at fault, replace it with an AGM unit and register the new battery with a diagnostic tool so the battery-management system uses the right charging strategy. Check for any outstanding software updates.
repairs.tools: Battery tester · basic sockets · LR047630 / LR176847 auxiliary battery · diagnostic tool for BMS registration

faq.q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
faq.a: On 20-inch wheels, the FullFatRR consensus is 285/50R20 (about 31.2 in). Two owners run them, one calls them probably the largest that won't rub in any height mode, and the spare still fits the well. 275/55R20 (about 31.9 in) is also fitted by 'quite a few' owners, though one member predicted it might just catch at full lock. Twenty inches is the smallest rim owners trust to clear the brakes, and 255/60R20 tyres on new-Defender wheels also fit. Want bigger? Lucky8 has a video on trimming the bumper for larger tyres on its lifted Project L405.

faq.q: What fuel economy should I expect?
faq.a: For the 2016 model year, the EPA rated the supercharged 5.0 V8 at 14 mpg city, 19 highway and 16 combined, the 3.0 supercharged V6 at 17/23/19, and the Td6 diesel at 22/28/24. PistonHeads reports about 30 mpg (UK) in real-world driving for the 4.4 SDV8.
Australian-market figures give 3,500 kg (7,716 lb) braked for the V8s, petrol or diesel, and 3,000 kg for the 3.0 V6s. Check your owner's manual and plate; the figure varies by engine and market.

What Car? calls the 3.0 TDV6 the sensible choice. PistonHeads rates the 4.4 SDV8 as 'a good and reliable engine' without the TDV6's crank issues or timing belt. In the US, the choice is the 5.0 V8 (thirsty, chain and coolant-pipe risks), the 3.0 V6, the Td6 diesel from 2016, or the later hybrids. AutoTrader.ca recommends a 2020-or-newer truck with the straight-six if budget allows.

faq.q: Is the TDV6 crankshaft failure real?
faq.a: Yes, but it isn't universal. Land Rover service bulletin SSM71816 (May 2014) blamed a 'low incidence' of crank failures mainly on wrongly located or rotating main-bearing shells. In a FullFatRR poll of L405 3.0 owners, 88% reported no issues. The usual advice is the correct oil, shorter oil-change intervals than the maximum, and a warranty that covers the engine.

Yes. Every L405 has permanent four-wheel drive with a Magna Steyr DD295 two-speed transfer case, a 50/50 split and a low range, managed by Terrain Response 2 with hill descent control. Change the transfer-box and diff oil at around 30,000 miles.

The easy way is height-sensor lift rods, which raise every air-suspension mode by 1, 1.5 or 2 inches with no electronics. Proud Rhino's rods take about 20–30 minutes to fit, and Lucky8 recommends an alignment afterwards.

faq.q: Can I work on the air suspension at home?
faq.a: Mostly, with the right scan tool. GAP's IID G4 tool lists air-suspension height adjustment and guided calibration for the L405. 2017–2022 trucks work with the standard tool, but 2013–2016 trucks need the optional adapter version. Struts and the compressor unbolt with hand tools, but the system runs at up to 10 bar, so depressurise it first, and the calibration afterwards needs the tool.

The 2018 facelift added the four-bar grille, new LED lights, thicker glass, Touch Pro Duo screens and the P400e plug-in hybrid. More importantly, PistonHeads says pre-2015 trucks had the most electrical and body faults. If budget allows, later is better.
Land Rover quoted 900 mm (35.4 in), 200 mm more than the L322, with up to 303 mm of ground clearance at off-road height.
Yes. Revealed at the 2013 LA Auto Show with deliveries from early 2014, it has a 3,122 mm (122.9 in) wheelbase and is 5,199 mm long — 200 mm more in each than the standard truck.

A hidden winch mount that tucks behind the factory bumper on the chassis and tow point, and a frame-mounted A-bar that fits standard and LWB trucks.

baseline_service.intro: Baseline everything, and before anything else run the VIN through Land Rover's recall lookup (the 2014–17 knuckle recall alone is worth it). Land Rover calls the ZF eight-speed 'filled for life' and gives the diffs and transfer box exact wet-fill volumes, so treat the official capacities below as the target and measure what goes in.

items.spec: Petrol 5.0 V8 / 3.0 V6 SC: 0W-20 to STJLR.51.5122 (the launch handbook listed 5W-20 to WSS-M2C925-A), 8.0 L for the V8 · TDV6/SDV6 (DPF): 5W-30 to STJLR.03.5005 / WSS-M2C934-B, 6.0 L · SDV8 (DPF): same spec, 9.4 L
items.interval: Then every 10,000 mi or sooner (owner practice); [CONFIRM IN MANUAL] for the factory schedule
items.note: The DPF diesels are fussy about oil, so only use oil approved to STJLR.03.5005. Don't overfill the SDV8: put in about 8.5 L, wait, then top up using the electronic level check.
